Title: Acute malnutrition among children 6-59 months and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) is reduced and infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices are improved in Upper Dir and Mardan districts, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Children 6-59 months with severe or moderate acute malnutrition are found early and recover through quality community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) that meets Sphere standards
Children 6-59 months are screened for acute malnutrition by MUAC and oedema check and referred
Monthly community MUAC and oedema screening by lady health workers and community volunteers
Refer screened SAM and MAM cases to OTP, SFP or stabilisation centre
Children with SAM without complications are treated in outpatient therapeutic programme (OTP) sites
Run OTP sites: admission, weekly RUTF distribution and follow-up
Children with MAM are treated in supplementary feeding programme (SFP) sites
Run SFP sites: ration distribution and follow-up
Children with SAM and medical complications are treated in stabilisation centres (SC)
Operate stabilisation centres: F-75, F-100 and ReSoMal treatment
Pregnant and lactating women are screened and treated, and caregivers practise optimal infant and young child feeding
PLW are screened and malnourished PLW are enrolled in supplementary feeding
Screen PLW by MUAC at health facilities and in the community and enrol malnourished PLW in SFP
PLW and caregivers receive IYCF counselling
IYCF counselling sessions at health facilities
IYCF counselling sessions in communities
Children 6-23 months and PLW receive micronutrient supplements
Distribute micronutrient powder (MNP) to children 6-23 months, and iron-folic acid (IFA) and multiple micronutrients (MMN) to PLW
Nutrition supplies and monthly data systems are reliable so that services do not stop
Nutrition supplies are received, stored and used without stock-outs
Manage nutrition supplies: RUTF, RUSF, F-75, F-100, ReSoMal, MNP, IFA and MUAC tapes
Monthly district nutrition data are complete, reviewed and reported on time
Monthly district data review, supportive supervision and training of health staff
